It is thought that millions of years ago these free-living prokaryotes were taken into larger cells by endocytosis where, instead of being digested, they became functional organelles. Which features of mitochondria and chloroplasts support this theory?
Mitochondria and chloroplasts synthesise proteins.

questions.questionText: Hydroxyproline is synthesised by addition of an –OH group to the R-group of the amino acid proline. Hydroxyproline is a major component of collagen and has an important role in increasing the stability of its structure. Which statement explains why the addition of an –OH group to proline could increase the stability of collagen?

options.A: It strengthens hydrogen bonding between the R-groups of adjacent polypeptide chains, resulting in a tertiary structure that is more resistant to heat denaturation.
options.B: It increases the number of sites available for the formation of hydrogen bonds within the secondary structure of collagen, resulting in more stable alpha helices.
options.C: It increases the formation of hydrogen bonds between R-groups and water molecules, which help to hold the chains of the collagen triple helix together by strengthening hydrophilic interactions.
options.D: It strengthens the quaternary structure of collagen by providing more sites for hydrogen bonding between the R-groups of distantly separated amino acids within the same polypeptide chain.

options.C: Cellulose and galactogen are both branched, but cellulose is a structural polysaccharide found in plants.
options.D: Amylopectin and galactogen are both storage polysaccharides, but amylopectin is formed from -glucose monomers.

Telomerase is an enzyme that prevents the shortening of telomeres. It is not present in most normal cells, but is active in an estimated 85% to 95% of human tumour cells. Which statement explains the effect of telomerase on human tumour cells?

options.A: Telomerase triggers a self-destruct process, known as apoptosis, ending the life of the cell.
options.B: Telomerase damages the chromosomes so they become genetically unstable and are unable to replicate and divide.
options.C: Telomerase helps human tumour cells avoid senescence, or cell death, which is usually the expected consequence of repeated cell division.
options.D: Telomerase enables the human tumour cells to divide more rapidly by reducing the time taken for a complete mitotic cell cycle.
